# Backplane pinout, draft 1 (generated by `backplane.js`, 2026-11-21)
Connector: **DIN 41612, 160 pins, 5 rows (z a b c d) × 32**, on 3U Eurocards. Signals: 112; GND: 32; +3V3: 12;
+5V: 4; spare: 0.

## Grouping
| group | pins | from → to |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| bus D0..D26 (dual-rail, 54 wires) | 54 | any card → any card; whoever the BUS field names drives, through 74LVC245s |
| micro-address UA0..UA9 | 10 | Control → every card |
| CLK, SCLK, RESET, /CEDGE, STRETCH, /WSTB | 6 | Control's clock and reset generator (cards/clockgen.js) → all. SCLK is the 40 MHz master clock (the Video card's slot clock, forwarded to the Memory card over J2); CLK = SCLK ÷ 4, or ÷ 8 when STRETCH (the carry-cycle stretch, driven by the ALU card from its control word); /CEDGE is low in the last slot of each CPU cycle; RESET is active high and releases on a CPU edge; /WSTB is the write strobe, low for one slot: slot 2 (slot 6 when stretched), so register RAM and main RAM write only once their address, data and ABORT have settled, and stop 25 ns before the CPU edge |
| FK | 1 | Memory → Control: which fault (protection or bad address), so the sequencer picks the right trap routine |
| SPRNR | 1 | Control → Registers, Memory: this SPR access is a latch, not a register-RAM slot; don't drive, don't write (Memory: don't snoop) |
| ABORT | 1 | Memory → all: the address check faulted this cycle, so no card may load anything (found by the ALU card's chip-level test) |
| LOAD, LOAD_WE, LOAD_SEL0..2 | 5 | copy engine (I/O card) → all: power-up table loading |
| status: SF±, CF±, QT±, BTOPNZ, BADADDR, PROT, IORDY, IRQSET0..4 | 15 | ALU / Memory / I/O / Video → Control (sequencer conditions). IRQSET0..2 come from the I/O card (timer, keyboard, mouse); IRQSET3/4 have no source on this machine and are pulled low |
| RSLOT0..4 | 5 | Control → Registers (register RAM slot); Memory snoops it to keep its UBASE/ULIMIT shadows |
| PORT0..5 | 6 | Control → I/O, Video (port number, through a small imm9→binary table) |
| MODE, PRIV, IE, PROTEN | 4 | Control → ALU (ESRV), Memory (PROTEN: user-window checks on; found building the Memory card), Video (MODE) |
| front panel | 4 | Front panel ↔ Control |

## Distributed control store
The 72-bit microword never crosses the backplane. **Only the 10-bit micro-address does.** Each card holds its own
control-store chips with just the fields it uses, plus its own pipeline register. A field more than one card needs
(BUS, PSW, the memory fields for Video) is a duplicate chip, not a wire. That saves 62 pins for 5 extra chips.
The ROM images get repacked per card by the ROM generator, and `verify-roms.js` re-checks them.

| card | fields | bits | 8-bit chips |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| Control | SEQ, COND, CONST, RF_SEL, LD_PC, LD_IR, PC, RETIRE, UCNT, PSW, IRQ_ACK, BUS | 39 | 5 |
| Registers | RF_RD, RF_WR, BUS | 6 | 1 |
| ALU | LD_A, LD_B, ALU_FN, ALU_FN_SRC, B_NEG, B_BCAST, CIN, SHIFT, WIDTH9, LD_QT, FLAGS, PSW, BUS | 28 | 4 |
| Memory | LD_MAR, LD_MDR, MDR_LANE, MAR_INC, MEM, BUS | 11 | 2 |
| IO | IO, BUS | 6 | 1 |
| Video | IO, BUS | 6 | 1 |
| **total** | (72-bit microword) | | **14** |

## Paths that ride the bus instead of getting pins (checked against the microcode)
- **Instruction fetch:** a memory read with LD_IR loads IR straight from RAM. All 4 control-store words that do this
  leave the bus idle (BUS = NONE), so the Memory card drives the tryte onto D0..D8 and Control latches it. No extra pins.
- **Video:** the framebuffer lives on the Memory card (option (a), Kham, 2026-11-18): VRAM-C for the CPU and a scan-out
  copy, VRAM-S, that the Video card reads over its own ribbon connector **J2** (not the backplane): SA0..18 in,
  SO0..11 out, VBUSY while a CPU framebuffer write owns VRAM-S, and a write port (SI0..11, /SWR) for the Video card's
  port-4 pixel and port-5 fill. The Video card only needs the IO and BUS fields now. See cards/MEMORY-CARD.md.
- **Bus contention:** every card decodes the same BUS field from the same micro-address, so exactly one card drives.
  Drivers get 33 Ω series resistors; 8 loads at 10 MHz.
